title: Tiny Solar Transmitters Track Butterflies in Eastern Taiwan, an Asian First
summaryZh: 花東縱谷為兩隻斑蝶裝上0.06克太陽能發射器，亞洲首例，民眾可用App協助追蹤。
summaryHi: पूर्वी ताइवान में दो तितलियों पर 0.06 ग्राम के सौर ट्रांसमीटर लगाए गए — एशिया में पहली बार; लोग ऐप से मदद कर सकते हैं।
summaryEs: En el este de Taiwán colocan a dos mariposas transmisores solares de 0,06 gramos, algo inédito en Asia; el público puede ayudar con una app.
summaryJa: 台湾東部で2匹のマダラチョウに0.06グラムの太陽光発信機を装着、アジア初。市民もアプリで追跡に協力できる。
summaryKo: 대만 동부에서 나비 두 마리에 0.06g 태양광 발신기를 부착했다. 아시아 최초이며 시민도 앱으로 추적을 도울 수 있다.
summaryEn: Researchers in eastern Taiwan fitted two butterflies with 0.06-gram solar transmitters, an Asian first, and invite the public to help track them.
paragraphs: Two butterflies in eastern Taiwan are now carrying miniature transmitters, making Taiwan the first place in Asia to track the insects this way. The East Longitudinal Valley National Scenic Area Headquarters, part of the Tourism Administration, announced the project on Wednesday together with several conservation groups.
The solar-powered devices weigh only 0.06 grams, small enough for a butterfly to carry. They give off a signal that smartphones within range can detect via Bluetooth.

So far, one small crow and one dark blue tiger have been tagged. Both belong to a group known as milkweed butterflies, which migrate to warmer valleys in the south each winter. Hung Chao-chang, the headquarters' deputy director, explained that earlier research relied on marking butterflies by hand and hoping to recapture them, which produced only scattered data. The transmitters, by contrast, allow the same individual to be followed throughout its life.

Speaking at Liyu Lake in Hualien County, Chan Chia-lung, president of the Taiwan Insect Habitat Protection Association, invited the public to take part. Anyone who installs the Project Monarch app and turns on Bluetooth and location services can help record the butterflies, and sightings can be reported with photos. He noted that a comparable project in the United States had tagged 400 monarch butterflies to follow their migration to Mexico.
Scientists in Taiwan put very small radios on two butterflies this week. This is the first time anyone in Asia has done this.
Each radio weighs only 0.06 grams. It uses power from the sun. It sends a signal to mobile phones near it.
The project is in Hualien, in the east of Taiwan. The butterflies are called the small crow and the dark blue tiger. In winter, they fly south to warm valleys.
Before, people had to catch the same butterfly again to learn about it. That was hard. Now phones can find the butterflies many times.
Anyone can help. You can get an app, turn on Bluetooth and send photos of the butterflies. In the United States, scientists did the same thing with 400 monarch butterflies.
sentZh: 台灣的科學家本週在兩隻蝴蝶身上裝上了非常小的無線電發射器。
這是亞洲第一次有人這麼做。
每個發射器只有 0.06 公克重。
它使用太陽的能量。
它會傳送訊號給附近的手機。
這個計畫在台灣東部的花蓮。
這兩種蝴蝶叫做小紫斑蝶和小青斑蝶。
冬天時，牠們會飛到南方溫暖的山谷。
以前，人們必須再抓到同一隻蝴蝶，才能了解牠。
那很困難。
現在手機可以很多次找到這些蝴蝶。
任何人都可以幫忙。
你可以下載一個應用程式、打開藍牙，並傳送蝴蝶的照片。
在美國，科學家曾對 400 隻帝王斑蝶做過同樣的事。

paragraphs: Researchers in eastern Taiwan have attached tiny transmitters to two butterflies, the first time this has been done in Asia. The project was announced on Wednesday by the East Longitudinal Valley National Scenic Area Headquarters, which worked with conservation groups.
Each transmitter weighs just 0.06 grams and runs on solar power. It sends a signal that nearby mobile phones can pick up through Bluetooth.

The two butterflies are a small crow and a dark blue tiger, both milkweed butterflies. According to Chan Chia-lung of the Taiwan Insect Habitat Protection Association, these butterflies move to warmer valleys in the south during winter.

Hung Chao-chang, a deputy director at the headquarters, said older studies depended on catching and marking butterflies by hand. Researchers rarely caught the same insect twice, so the records were incomplete. With the new tags, the same butterfly can be detected again and again.

Members of the public can join in as citizen scientists. They need to install the Project Monarch app, switch on Bluetooth and location, and send in photos with the time and place. A similar project in the United States tracked 400 monarch butterflies on their journey to Mexico.

paragraphs: In what organisers describe as an Asian first, researchers in eastern Taiwan have fitted two wild butterflies with featherweight radio transmitters. The initiative, unveiled on Wednesday by the East Longitudinal Valley National Scenic Area Headquarters, brings together tourism officials and conservationists.

Weighing a mere 0.06 grams and powered by sunlight, each tag emits a signal that any smartphone in range can pick up over Bluetooth. The first two subjects are a small crow and a dark blue tiger, milkweed species that retreat to sheltered southern valleys when temperatures drop.

According to deputy director Hung Chao-chang, conventional mark-and-recapture methods yielded fragmented records, since a tagged insect was seldom found a second time. Electronic tracking, he said, makes it possible to detect the same butterfly repeatedly over its entire life cycle.

Crucially, the scheme depends on ordinary people. Chan Chia-lung, who heads the Taiwan Insect Habitat Protection Association, urged residents and visitors to download the Project Monarch app, enable Bluetooth and location tracking, and submit dated photographs of any sightings.
The approach mirrors an American study that equipped 400 monarch butterflies with similar devices to chart their long journey to Mexico.
sentZh: 主辦單位稱這是亞洲首例：東台灣的研究人員為兩隻野生蝴蝶裝上了極輕的無線電發射器。
這項計畫由花東縱谷國家風景區管理處於週三公布，結合了觀光官員與保育人士。
每個標籤僅重 0.06 公克，以陽光供電，會發出訊號，範圍內任何智慧型手機都能透過藍牙接收。
首批兩個研究對象是一隻小紫斑蝶和一隻小青斑蝶，這兩種斑蝶會在氣溫下降時退到南部避風的山谷。
副處長洪肇昌表示，傳統的標記再捕法只能得到片段的紀錄，因為被標記的昆蟲很少會再次被找到。
他說，電子追蹤讓研究人員能在蝴蝶整個生命週期中反覆偵測到同一隻。
關鍵在於，這項計畫仰賴一般民眾。
台灣昆蟲棲地保護協會理事長詹家龍呼籲居民和遊客下載 Project Monarch 應用程式，開啟藍牙和定位追蹤，並提交註明日期的目擊照片。
這種做法仿效了美國一項研究，該研究為 400 隻帝王斑蝶裝上類似裝置，以描繪牠們前往墨西哥的漫長旅程。

paragraphs: Taiwan has become the first country in Asia to monitor migrating butterflies with miniature electronic tags, after researchers in Hualien attached solar-powered transmitters to two specimens this week. The project is coordinated by the East Longitudinal Valley National Scenic Area Headquarters in collaboration with conservation organisations.

Each device weighs a negligible 0.06 grams and transmits a signal detectable by nearby smartphones via Bluetooth. The two tagged insects, a small crow and a dark blue tiger, are milkweed butterflies whose seasonal migration takes them to warmer valleys further south.

Deputy director Hung Chao-chang acknowledged the limitations of traditional fieldwork, in which butterflies were marked by hand and only occasionally recaptured, leaving substantial gaps in the data. Continuous electronic detection, he argued, could provide a far more comprehensive picture of each individual's life cycle.

A distinctive feature of the scheme is its reliance on citizen science. Chan Chia-lung of the Taiwan Insect Habitat Protection Association encouraged the public to install a dedicated app and report sightings, effectively turning every phone into a mobile receiving station.

The method is modelled on a North American programme that tracked 400 monarch butterflies on their migration to Mexico, and researchers hope it will reveal precisely how Taiwan's butterflies survive the winter.
sentZh: 台灣成為亞洲第一個以微型電子標籤監測遷徙蝴蝶的國家，花蓮的研究人員本週為兩隻蝴蝶裝上了太陽能發射器。
這項計畫由花東縱谷國家風景區管理處與保育組織合作協調。
每個裝置僅重微不足道的 0.06 公克，並發出可被附近智慧型手機透過藍牙偵測到的訊號。
這兩隻被標記的昆蟲——一隻小紫斑蝶和一隻小青斑蝶——都是斑蝶，季節性遷徙會帶牠們前往更南方較溫暖的山谷。
副處長洪肇昌坦承傳統田野調查的侷限：蝴蝶以人工標記，只是偶爾被再次捕獲，導致資料出現大量缺口。
他認為，持續的電子偵測能更全面地呈現每隻蝴蝶的生命週期。
這項計畫的一大特色是仰賴公民科學。
台灣昆蟲棲地保護協會的詹家龍鼓勵民眾安裝專用應用程式並回報目擊，實際上讓每支手機都成為行動接收站。
這個方法仿照北美一項追蹤 400 隻帝王斑蝶遷徙到墨西哥的計畫，研究人員希望藉此精確了解台灣的蝴蝶如何度過冬天。
